chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Duke Ellington, Jimmie Lunceford and Count Basie
summary: Howard knew Ellington well, found Lunceford quiet and serious and not much of a player, and says Basie played piano alone at the union.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you know any of the people well, like Duke and Jimmie Lunceford?
Well, yeah, I knew Duke well. Go out there and you'll see a picture Duke set up for me and said some nice things on it.
I bet, yeah. What about Jimmie
Jimmie Lunceford? Jimmie wasn't very friendly.
He wasn't, eh?
No, not too much.
A little quieter man, right?
Very quiet.
A very serious man.
Huh?
He seemed to be a very serious man, Jimmie.
He was a very serious man.
Yeah.
Very quiet. I used to love to see him playing.
Jimmie play?
Huh?
You used to love to see Jimmie play?
Yeah. I used to love to see Jimmie play.
What did he play?
He played the -- I don't think he did much playing of any instrument.
They said he was a flute player but I didn't see him play much either.
No, I didn't see him. He didn't play
much. Now it comes out.
What's that?
I said it comes out now.
Yeah.
He didn't play anything, see.
Yeah, but in a couple of pictures he had a flute on the stand next to him, but I don't know whether and maybe he could play it, but he didn't play it very much.
No, he didn't play much at all.
Yeah, well, I'm glad to know. What about Basie, did they do the same thing?
No, Basie didn't play anything.
No, but I mean -- Basie played piano though, but did they rehearse at the union like --
No, he'd sit down and play piano.
By himself.
Huh?
By himself?
Yeah.
But not bring in the whole band.
No, he didn't bring in the whole band, no. He'd be playing by himself.
Well, very good. That's -- you had some- thing.
